mechanism_narrative: A sustained two-week rise in TRANSIT and PARKS mobility signals increased outdoor and commuting activity that lifts weekday retail footfall, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -35.0 to -32.9 and PARKS from -31.1 to -23.4 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days when TRANSIT and PARKS both rise week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean crosses above -5.0 (less negative), it signals reduced panic buying and a shift toward discretionary retail spending, raising RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean rises above -5.0 from below -5.0
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM recovered from -7.4 at t-1w to -5.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -5.0 and RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days does not increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility combined with stable WORKPLACES indicates people returning to work and leisure, which increases retail footfall and drives higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.

failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL declines and WORKPLACES is stable, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls, the hypothesis is rejected.
